label: Q01
question: Thirteen TOC values lie between 2,077 and 2,208 umol/L, 20 to 60 times the median (61.5 umol/L) and in the range of seawater dissolved inorganic carbon. Are they valid, or did inorganic carbon survive the acidification/sparging step?
context: Observed in table_253.csv (EDI rev 3, 2026-10-06): 99th percentile 111 umol/L; 20 further values lie between 300 and 800 umol/L. The 13 values come from 5 cruises 2015-07 to 2017-08, at both inshore (e.g. 2015-10-29-C-32OC cast 28, line 86.7 station 33, four depths 2-51 m, 2,077-2,103 umol/L) and offshore stations (2017-08-01-C-33SR cast 42, line 86.7 station 100, 85 m, 2,089 umol/L). The ingest publishes them as-is until this is answered. Only valid_min = 0 is registered for toc; no upper bound is set. Checked 2026-10-06 against calcofi_dic in release v2026.10.05: dissolved inorganic carbon on the same five cruises runs about 1,970-2,060 umol/kg at 0-15 m, 2,020-2,210 at 61-150 m, 2,130-2,260 at 151-250 m and 2,210-2,350 below 250 m, the same range as these 13 values (2,077-2,208 umol/L at 2-440 m), and about 35 times the TOC median. Still published unflagged until confirmed.
proposed_answer: They are not TOC: inorganic carbon was not removed (or the sample was mislabeled), so the values are effectively DIC. Exclude them from the published TOC unless you have corrected values.

label: Q02
question: 50 bottles carry more than one TOC row (46 with 2, 4 with 4). Are these replicate analyses of one water sample? In 2014-07-06-C-32NM cast 21, bottles 3 and 4 (both 3,498 m) list the same four values (40.4, 45.7, 46.3, 50.6 umol/L): are those four analyses split across the two bottles?
context: The ingest keeps one sample per bottle and publishes every row as its own obs (not averaged), so a bottle with replicates has 2 or 4 toc values. Some replicate pairs differ a lot, e.g. 2008-08-14-C-32NM cast 9 bottle 20 at 10 m: 60.0 and 81.1 umol/L.

label: Q03
question: What does 'TOC CV (%)' measure?
context: 59 rows have no CV; 6 exceed 10%, up to 43.8%.
answer: Coefficient of variation: the standard deviation divided by the mean, x 100 (CV = SD / mean x 100); the spread of the analysis relative to the reported TOC. The ingest publishes it as each value's precision, measurement_prec = TOC x CV / 100 (the SD in umol/L); NULL on the 59 rows with no CV.

label: Q04
question: What is 'Associated Bottle number'? It differs from 'Bottle number' on 22 rows. Which is the bottle the water came from?
context: The EML definition repeats the column name. The ingest keys samples on Bottle number and does not publish Associated Bottle number. Example: 2008-08-14-C-32NM cast 68, Bottle number 13 vs Associated Bottle number 14 at 10 m. Checked 2026-10-06: the HPLC table from the same program (EDI knb-lter-cce.316.1) defines 'Associated Bottle Number' in its EML as the 'CTD rosette niskin bottle number CalCOFI sampled; must use to integrate with CalCOFI bottle data', and 'Bottle Number' as the 'reference number of sample bottle from rosette'.
proposed_answer: Bottle number is the rosette bottle the water was drawn from; Associated Bottle number is the CalCOFI bottle whose bottle-data record the sample pairs with (the definition in the HPLC EML, knb-lter-cce.316.1). Keep keying samples on Bottle number.

label: Q05
question: One row (2009-01-08-C-32NM, line 93.3 station 60, cast 11, bottle 19, 66.4 umol/L) has the date '0000-00-00 00:00:00', no latitude/longitude and depth 'NULL'. Can you supply its time, position and depth?
context: Held out of the release until supplied: time, position and depth are coordinates in the integrated database and are never guessed. Checked 2026-10-06: the other TOC rows of the same cast (2009-01-08-C-32NM cast 11) are timed 2009-01-09 14:23:00 GMT at 31.85N 119.57W, and release v2026.10.05 has exactly that calcofi_bottle cast (calcofi_bottle:cast:31985, 093.3 060.0, same time and position, cruise 2009-01-32NM). On that cast bottle 20 is at 2 m and bottle 15 at 50 m; the bottle database has bottles at 10, 20, 30 and 40 m between them, so bottles 16-19 are 40, 30, 20 and 10 m. The neighbouring cast 10 on the same cruise uses exactly that pattern (bottle 19 at 10 m).
proposed_answer: Time 2009-01-09 14:23:00 GMT, position 31.85N 119.57W (from cast 11's other rows and the matching calcofi_bottle cast); depth 10 m (bottle 19, by rosette order). The row stays held out until confirmed.

label: Q06
question: On 2017-01-06-C-33RL cast 37 (33.65N, 118.97W), bottles 1 and 2 are at 725 m and 720 m, but the seafloor there is about 657 m (701 m in the deepest neighbouring cell of the GEBCO 2025 grid). Is the position or the depth right?
context: Found 2026-10-07 by the depth-vs-seafloor check (calcofi4db check_depth_vs_seafloor(), +10 m tolerance). The position is given to 0.01 degree (about 1 km) on a steep slope, so it may be position precision rather than a wrong depth. Both samples are published as given; nothing is deleted.
